blurb: An asset is a name for a file, read as a value (`style.url`), so a unit declares each name once: a second `asset style` would leave `style` meaning two files. Give each asset its own name, or drop the repeat when it names the same file. An asset whose name is a function's or a type's is `bynk.resolve.name_conflict` instead.
example:
asset style = "assets/board.css"
asset style = "assets/print.css"    // ✗ `style` is already declared

asset style = "assets/board.css"
asset print = "assets/print.css"    // ✓ one name each
summary: An `asset` name is declared more than once in the same unit.
